Answer: B
Reason: In the context of high-speed trauma, a widened mediastinum and specifically the blurring or indistinctness of the aortic knob are classic radiographic signs suggestive of traumatic aortic injury (such as an aortic transection or hematoma). While other findings like tracheal deviation or apical caps can be associated with thoracic trauma, the loss of definition of the aortic arch is most directly indicative of pathology involving the aorta itself.
